headline: Tech rout and tame Canada CPI lift the dollar to a 19-month high; euro tests 1.10
summary: The dollar index edged up to about 103.5, its highest since April 2025, as a 2.5% Nasdaq slide on Nvidia's leadership crisis sent investors to the high-yielding dollar and a December Fed hike stayed about 90% priced, even as short-dated yields slipped. The loonie, Aussie, peso and rupiah lagged, with the rupiah at a record low, while the rupee, yuan and won held firm on inflows and exporter selling.
drivers: The S&P 500 fell 1.9% and the Nasdaq 2.5% as Nvidia's board ruled out bringing back its former CEO, and the Kospi lost 3.6%. The euro slipped to about 1.0999, a 19-month low, and the Aussie fell about 0.5% to near 0.6735, a 10-month low.
Fed hike bets hold; Canada and oil hit the loonie

A 25bp Fed hike on Dec 9 stays about 90% priced; Warsh skipped policy, and Hammack prefers small steps, cooling 50bp talk. Tamer Canadian CPI and a 3.6% drop in Brent to $92.44 sent USD/CAD to about 1.4310, a 19-month high.

Taiwan's central bank stepped in as foreign selling pushed USD/TWD to 32.969, and the rupiah closed at a record 18,268. The rupee rose 27 paise to 93.92 on equity inflows, and exporters kept the won and yuan firm.
view: Still bullish for the next 1–2 weeks: the Fed is set to hike in December while the BoC and RBA look done and the ECB is near the end, and the tech selloff adds haven demand, so I keep backing the dollar against the loonie, Aussie and euro. I fade it only against the yen near 160, where Tokyo is on watch and the BoJ may hike. A DXY close back below 102.5, a strong Nvidia report that revives risk appetite, or Fed speakers ruling out more hikes would turn me neutral.
ideas: Hold the long from 1.4080–1.4100 as tame CPI keeps the BoC on hold; for 1.4450, stop raised to 1.4240.
Hold the short from 1.1170–1.1190 after the break of 1.10; target extended to 1.0900, stop cut to 1.1060.
Hold the sale filled at 160.00–160.20 as Tokyo guards 160; for 157.50, stop cut to 160.70.
review: The dollar calls gained again: the EUR/USD short is about 180 pips in favour, AUD/USD about 175 and USD/CAD about 210, so I trail stops and extend targets; the USD/JPY sale is about 60 pips up and the ringgit and rupiah longs are slightly ahead. USD/CHF closed on its 0.8400 cap and turns long, EUR/JPY slipped under 175.5 and turns short, and all other ranges held.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.2% to near 1.0999, a fresh 19-month low; the short is about 180 pips in favour.
eurusd.why: The dollar did the moving. A 2.5% Nasdaq slide on Nvidia's leadership turmoil pushed investors into the high-yielding dollar, and Fed hike bets held even as short-dated Treasury yields slipped about 4bp. The ECB set its reference rate at 1.1014, and with no fresh euro news the pair tested 1.10 for the first time since April 2025.
eurusd.outlook: I hold the short, extend the target to 1.0900 and trail the stop to 1.1060: the Fed is still outpacing an ECB near the end of its cycle. A close back above 1.1060 would say the dollar's rally has stalled.
eurusd.watch: German ZEW and ECB's Lane and Cipollone (Nov 17), Nvidia results (Nov 17), euro zone flash PMIs (late Nov).

view.call: Short from 1.1170–1.1190; Fed outpaces a late-cycle ECB.

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.15% to near 1.3186, a fifth straight loss and a five-week low, inside my 1.3150–1.3350 range.
gbpusd.why: The dollar did the moving. Sterling had no UK data of its own, and weekend hawkish remarks from BoE's Pill and Greene were already priced, so the pound simply tracked the dollar's risk-off rally. It held up better than the euro and Aussie because a second BoE hike on Dec 17 is still seen as likely.
gbpusd.outlook: I keep the 1.3150–1.3350 range, but the risk is to the downside: a soft UK jobs or CPI print would break 1.3150 and turn me bearish toward the 2026 lows. Firm wages and a 3.7% or higher CPI would lift it back toward 1.33.
gbpusd.watch: UK jobs (Nov 17), UK CPI and Bailey (Nov 18), UK retail sales (Nov 20), BoE (Dec 17).

view.call: 1.3150–1.3350; BoE hike bets vs firm Fed.

audusd.note: Down about 0.5% to near 0.6735, a new 10-month low; the sale is about 175 pips in favour.
audusd.why: Both sides moved. The Aussie, the market's main risk proxy, fell as the Nasdaq dropped 2.5% and Korean stocks lost over 3%, while option traders paid the most for Aussie puts since April. At home, the RBA's split 6–3 vote to hike to 4.85% points to a pause, so the rate gap keeps moving the dollar's way.
audusd.outlook: I hold the sale, extend the target to 0.6650 and cut the stop to 0.6790: the RBA looks done, the Fed is hiking and the 0.6749 Fibonacci support has given way. A close above 0.6790, perhaps on a strong Nvidia report or jobs data, would end the call.
audusd.watch: RBA minutes and Nvidia results (Nov 17), wages (Nov 18), jobs (Nov 19), monthly CPI (Nov 25).

view.call: Sale from 0.6900–0.6920; RBA paused, Fed hiking.

usdjpy.note: Down about 0.1% to near 159.47; my sale from 160.00–160.20 is about 60 pips in favour.
usdjpy.why: The yen did the moving, slightly. Japan's economy shrank 0.1% annualised in the third quarter against 0.3% growth expected, but traders looked past it as Capital Economics and others still see a BoJ hike in December. The stock rout and fear of intervention near 160 led traders to trim yen shorts, offsetting the firm dollar.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the sale for 157.50 and cut the stop to 160.70, just above Friday's 160.19 spike: Tokyo is guarding 160 and the BoJ may hike in December. A close above 160.70 would show officials are standing aside.
usdjpy.watch: Tokyo comments near 160, Nvidia results (Nov 17), Japan CPI (Nov 20), BoJ speakers, US yields.

view.call: Sale filled 160.00–160.20; Tokyo guards 160, BoJ may hike.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.15% to near 0.8400, a 19-month high, right on my 0.8400 range top.
usdchf.why: The dollar did the moving. Fed hike bets keep the rate gap wide while the SNB holds at 0%, which makes the franc a funding currency for carry trades. Even a 2% drop in the S&P 500 gave the franc little haven support, because higher US yields and the dollar's own haven appeal won out.
usdchf.outlook: The close on the 0.8400 cap turns me long toward 0.8500 with a stop at 0.8340: the rate gap favours the dollar and the franc is no longer acting as a haven. A close back below 0.8340 would say the break has failed.
usdchf.watch: Fed speakers, SNB comments, equity sentiment, Swiss inflation (early Dec).

view.call: Long 0.8380–0.8400; rate gap, franc used to fund carry.

usdcad.note: Up about 0.25% to near 1.4299 after a 19-month high of about 1.4310; the buy is about 210 pips in favour.
usdcad.why: Both sides moved. Canada's October CPI came in tamer than expected, so economists such as CIBC now see the BoC holding in December, while the Fed is set to hike. Oil added to the loonie's losses: Brent settled 3.6% lower at $92.44 as Hormuz flows recover, and Canada's 10-year yield fell about 4bp to 3.82%.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the buy for 1.4450 and raise the stop to 1.4240, under Monday's lows, to lock in most of the gain: the BoC looks done and the Fed is not. A sharp oil rebound or a dovish Fed turn would be the main risks.
usdcad.watch: BoC speakers, oil and Hormuz headlines, Fed speakers, Canada retail sales (late Nov).

view.call: Long from 1.4080–1.4100; tame CPI, BoC on hold, Fed hiking.

usdcnh.note: Down about 0.15% to near 6.665 offshore as exporters sold dollars despite a still-weak PBOC fixing.
usdcnh.why: Exporter flows did the moving. The PBOC set the midpoint at 6.7141, about 370 pips weaker than the 6.6771 estimate, and the higher FX reserve ratio took effect, yet year-end dollar selling by exporters kept the yuan firm. Soft October data, with industrial output up 4.8%, did little to the currency.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: the PBOC leans against gains while exporters sell dollars on rallies. A close below 6.64 would show Beijing is letting the rally run; above 6.70 would show it wants a weaker yuan.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, loan prime rates (Nov 20), US-China summit headlines.

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC slows the yuan, exporters sell USD.

usdhkd.note: Steady near 7.8466, about 35 pips from the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved the pair. The gap between US rates and one-month HIBOR, about 2.68%, keeps the carry trade into US dollars attractive and holds the Hong Kong dollar near the weak end of its band. Banks' heavy use of the HKMA discount window shows liquidity is tight, which limits how far the pair can rise.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: the carry gap keeps it near 7.85, and only a jump in HIBOR or HKMA buying at 7.85 would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, Fed speakers.

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Up about 0.05% to near 1.2888, inside my 1.2780–1.2920 range.
usdsgd.why: The dollar did the moving. Fed hike bets and the global tech selloff kept the dollar firm across Asia, but the Singapore dollar lost far less than its neighbours. UOB estimates the S$NEER is about 1.6% above the middle of the MAS band, so the policy path still supports it.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2780–1.2920 range: the MAS band limits losses, but a Fed set to hike keeps the pair firm. A close above 1.2920 would open a long toward 1.3000; UOB sees support near 1.2840.
usdsgd.watch: Singapore final Q3 GDP and non-oil exports, Fed speakers, Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won rose 1.0 to 1,335.7 in Seoul even as the Kospi fell 3.6%; offshore about 1,335.6.
usdkrw.why: Exporters did the moving. The Kospi lost 3.59% to 5,100.5 as foreigners sold tech shares over the Nvidia fallout, which would normally hurt the won. Exporters' dollar sales absorbed the outflows and lower oil helped Korea's import bill, so the won held near the strong end of its recent range.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep the 1,330–1,365 range: exporter selling favours the won, but foreign stock selling and a Fed set to hike limit gains. A Seoul close below 1,325 would open 1,315; above 1,365 would revive the long.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, Nvidia results (Nov 17), oil and Hormuz headlines, Fed speakers.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar fell 4.8 cents to 32.886 in Taipei after trading 32.870–32.969; offshore near 32.96 later.
usdtwd.why: Equity outflows did the moving. The Taiex plunged more than 2,600 points as US tech stocks slid, and heavy foreign selling pushed the pair through 32.9. Local reports said the central bank stepped in near the close, trimming a loss of more than 10 cents to 4.8 cents.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep the 32.60–33.05 range: officials are defending 33 again, but foreign selling and Fed hikes cap the Taiwan dollar's gains. A close above 33.05 would show the defence has failed; below 32.60 would open 32.40.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, Nvidia results (Nov 17), central bank action near 33, Fed speakers.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit eased to 4.0915/0960 at the 6pm KL close from 4.0845/0890; my long is slightly in favour.
usdmyr.why: The dollar did the moving. Bank Muamalat said futures fully price a December Fed hike with some chance of 50bp, which lifted demand for dollars across Asia. The ringgit still rose against most major and ASEAN currencies, so the weakness was about the dollar rather than Malaysia.
usdmyr.outlook: I hold the long, extend the target to 4.125 and raise the stop to 4.075: Fed hike bets outweigh Bank Negara's steady rate for now. A close back below 4.075 would say the break has failed.
usdmyr.watch: Bank Negara comments, regional chip stocks, oil, Fed speakers.

view.call: Long 4.080–4.090; break of 4.085 on Fed hike bets.

usdphp.note: Peso fell 22 centavos to 63.94 at the BAP close, a fourth straight loss and near its record low.
usdphp.why: The dollar did the moving. RCBC's chief economist pointed to Fed hike bets, high Treasury yields and geopolitical risk, and the PSEi's 2% drop to pandemic-era lows added to stagflation worries. Lower oil, with Brent down 3.6%, gave little relief during Manila hours.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 63.30–64.20 range with the record low as the cap: possible BSP hikes and holiday remittances help, but the Fed weighs. A close above 64.20 would mark a new record and open 64.80.
usdphp.watch: BSP comments, oil and Hormuz headlines, Fed speakers, BSP decision (Dec 17).

usdidr.note: Rupiah fell 62 points to 18,268, a record weak close; JISDOR 18,250. My long is about 40 points up.
usdidr.why: Both sides moved. A stronger dollar on Fed hike bets met local worries: government interest costs have reached Rp494tn so far this year, and political uncertainty after last week's vice-presidential resignation persists. The rupiah fell even though Bank Indonesia had defended it on Friday.
usdidr.outlook: I hold the long for 18,500 and raise the stop to 18,150: Fed bets, MSCI-related outflows and politics outweigh BI's smoothing. A hawkish BI move this week that pulls it back below 18,150 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Bank Indonesia decision (Nov 18–19), MSCI changes (effective Nov 30), politics, Fed speakers.

view.call: Long 18,200–18,250; Fed, politics and outflows vs BI.

usdinr.note: Rupee rose 27 paise to 93.92, Asia's best performer, trading 93.91–94.25.
usdinr.why: Flows did the moving. Foreign buying of Indian shares and a rally in local stocks lifted the rupee against the regional trend, and softer oil eased importers' dollar needs. DBS noted steady equity and debt inflows; high US yields and the firm dollar capped the gain.
usdinr.outlook: I keep the 93.50–94.50 range: inflows help the rupee, but state-bank dollar buying and the Fed cap it. A close below 93.50 would open 93.00; above 94.50 would open 95.
usdinr.watch: RBI decision (Dec 4), oil and Hormuz headlines, foreign equity flows, Fed speakers.

eurjpy.note: Down about 0.4% to near 175.4, just under my 175.5 range floor, as the euro fell and the yen firmed.
eurjpy.why: Both sides moved. The euro slid to a 19-month low against the dollar, while the yen gained as the stock rout and intervention fears near 160 led traders to cut short yen bets. Japan's surprise GDP contraction did not shake expectations of a BoJ hike in December.
eurjpy.outlook: The close below 175.5 turns me short toward 174.0 with a stop at 176.3: the euro is losing ground and the yen is protected by Tokyo and BoJ hike bets. A close back above 176.3 would say the range has resumed.
eurjpy.watch: Tokyo comments, ECB's Lane (Nov 17), Japan CPI (Nov 20), euro zone PMIs.

view.call: Sell 175.4–175.8; weak euro, yen guarded near 160.

cnhjpy.note: Little changed near 23.93, in the upper half of my 23.6–24.2 range.
cnhjpy.why: Both sides firmed together. The yuan gained about 0.15% against the dollar on exporter selling, and the yen firmed slightly on intervention fears, so the cross barely moved. The PBOC's weak fixing and Tokyo's warnings keep both currencies anchored.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.6–24.2 range: the yuan is held steady, so the cross follows USD/JPY, which Tokyo is likely to cap near 160. A close above 24.2 would show intervention is not coming.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, Tokyo comments near 160, Japan CPI (Nov 20).

view.call: 23.6–24.2; yen near Tokyo's line, yuan held.

eurcnh.note: Down about 0.3% to near 7.33 as the euro fell and the yuan firmed.
eurcnh.why: Both sides moved it lower. The euro slid to a 19-month low against the dollar on risk aversion and Fed hike bets, while exporters' dollar sales lifted the yuan. The PBOC's weak fixings slow the yuan's gains, but they do not stop the cross from following the euro.
eurcnh.outlook: I keep a 7.28–7.40 range with a downward tilt: euro weakness should continue, but the PBOC is leaning against yuan strength. A close below 7.28 would open 7.22.
eurcnh.watch: PBOC fixings, ECB speakers, euro zone PMIs, China data.

view.call: 7.28–7.40; weak euro vs PBOC brake on yuan.

watch: Next: UK jobs, RBA minutes, Nvidia results and ECB's Lane (Nov 17), UK CPI and Australian wages (Nov 18), Bank Indonesia (Nov 18–19), Australia jobs (Nov 19), Japan CPI (Nov 20), then the RBI (Dec 4), Fed (Dec 8–9) and BoE and BSP (Dec 17), plus Tokyo's 160 line and Taiwan's defence of 33.
sources: Reuters via Business Times (yen, Japan GDP)
